title: Gandhi's Indigo Truth
subtitle: How a quiet investigation turned indigo fear into a record the Raj could not ignore
moral: Truth grows powerful when it is patiently recorded.

sources.citation: M.K. Gandhi, An Autobiography: The Story of My Experiments with Truth, Part V, Champaran chapters
sources.note: Participant account of the inquiry, arrest and settlement.

sources.citation: Government of Bihar and Orissa, Report of the Champaran Agrarian Enquiry Committee (1917)
sources.note: Official record acknowledging planter abuses and recommending reform.

sources.citation: Jacques Pouchepadass, Champaran and Gandhi: Planters, Peasants and Gandhian Politics (1999)
sources.note: Modern reconstruction using planter and district records.

panels.shot: medium close-up on Gandhi and Shukla at a railway platform, steam around them, Shukla gripping Gandhi’s arm as the train waits

dialogue.speaker: Raj Kumar Shukla
dialogue.text: Bapu, come see our fields. Indigo has chained us.

panels.shot: bird’s-eye wide of Champaran countryside showing scattered villages, indigo patches, and a distant planter factory chimney

dialogue.text: Champaran was not a battlefield, but a patchwork of estates where tenants, tied by tinkathia, had to grow indigo on fixed land even when the blue dye had lost its shine on world markets.

panels.shot: intimate interior shot inside a peasant hut, Gandhi seated on a low stool as a tenant couple speaks nervously

dialogue.text: He did not start with slogans. He started with listening, as tenants haltingly told him how planters forced indigo on their best land, fined them for refusing, and demanded illegal payments when synthetic dyes ruined the old profits.

panels.shot: wide shot outside the courthouse as a crowd waits; an official emerges to announce postponement and no immediate sentencing

dialogue.text: The case hung in the air. Officials hesitated to jail a man who broke the law so openly, yet so politely. They postponed sentence and quietly let him continue his work.

panels.shot: wide shot of a government meeting room in Patna, with the Champaran enquiry committee seated at a long table, Gandhi among them

dialogue.text: Under rising pressure, the provincial government formed an enquiry committee. Gandhi accepted a seat, carrying into the room not anger, but stacks of detailed testimonies.
